title: Presentism as an Empirical Hypothesis
locators: pp. 1101–1111, especially opening premises P1/P2 and p. 1108 discussion of the epistemic and ontological interpretation of relativistic spacetime; author-linked draft indexed at https://www.kbrading.org/papers
assumptions: Brading states P1 (only what exists now is real) alongside P2 (special relativity is a complete account of spatiotemporal structure), and retains P2. Her move revises the epistemic-versus-ontological role assigned to that complete physical spacetime account, rather than rejecting SR completeness. Her law-constitutive account of unity allows a present region sized to sustain a dynamical system without selecting a global simultaneity slice.
conclusion: The paper argues that accepting SR's complete account of empirical spatiotemporal structure does not by itself settle the ontological reading in favor of a block. It proposes a presentist core tied to dynamical unity and system-sustaining regions. It supplies no new field equation, parameter, preparation, detector, or quantitative signature. Its claim that the alternative remains unfalsified is a philosophical assessment, not an experimental result.
proof_status: Full paper text screened from the author-linked draft/search-indexed text and bibliographic record; no independent argument reconstruction.
dependencies: Newtonian law-constitutive unity via DiSalle; special-relativistic causal/spatiotemporal structure; no new physical model supplied.
open_questions: What independently specified physical theory and measurement would falsify the law-constitutive presentist interpretation? The 2013 paper supplies no concrete test; distinguish this from the 2015 follow-up's claim that refutation would require resources beyond SR.
relevance: Required exact audit of Brading's proposal; shows it is not a quantitative discriminator between temporal ontologies.
limits: Philosophical proposal rather than experimental protocol. A relational/dynamical notion of which region sustains a system does not by itself determine whether past/future entities exist or whether passage is objective.

title: Physically Locating the Present: A Case of Reading Physics as a Contribution to Philosophy
version: Studies in History and Philosophy of Science Part A 50 (2015), 13–19; DOI 10.1016/j.shpsa.2014.09.007
locators: Abstract and indexed text for Sec. 3 and conclusion; not full text audited
assumptions: A law-constitutive account of unity is drawn from Newtonian physics and transposed as an interpretive approach within relativistic spacetime.
conclusion: The abstract says the approach need not preserve all contemporary presentist desiderata and that, if empirically refuted, it would require resources beyond special relativity. Indexed text characterizes the present of a dynamical system as a spatiotemporal region of whatever size is needed to sustain it. This beyond-SR remark belongs to the 2015 follow-up; it is not Brading's 2013 move, which retains SR's completeness while revising its ontological interpretation.
proof_status: Abstract-level primary source; full article not inspected.
dependencies: Brading 2013; Newtonian law-constitutive unity; special relativity.
open_questions: How are overlapping systems' presents unified, and what independent empirical theory tests the account?
relevance: Clarifies the empirically open status claim and the concrete shape of the proposed present.
limits: No operational falsifier or quantitative prediction extracted; the localized present is not an experimentally established preferred frame.

title: Quantum Time: Experimental Multi-Time Correlations
locators: arXiv abstract and APS abstract; full methods not audited
assumptions: Page–Wootters decomposition of a stationary global state into clock and system; narrow-band single photon, with photon's position encoding clock reading; internal observer conditions on clock position and tests two-time correlations.
conclusion: Authors report an experimental illustration of the Page–Wootters mechanism, two-time quantum correlations and an internal-view Leggett–Garg inequality violation, while an external description treats the global state as time-independent over the experiment timescale.
proof_status: Abstract and experimental claim inspected; raw data and detailed optical protocol not independently audited or reproduced.
dependencies: Page and Wootters (1983); Leggett–Garg inequality; narrow-band single-photon optics.
open_questions: How robust is the claim to finite wavepacket width, detector resolution, and alternate external-time models? What outcomes distinguish ontologies rather than clock-conditioned and unconditioned descriptions?
relevance: An actual quantum-clock proposal/realization, not merely a formal construction.
limits: Tests correlation structure and clock-conditioned predictions inside standard quantum optics. It does not test global timelessness, fundamental time emergence, or presentism versus eternalism; both external and relational descriptions are admitted.

title: Unveiling Emergent Internal Time from Entropy Exchange in a Cold-Atom System
version: arXiv:2509.07745v2, 2026-03-16; published as "Testing the problem of time with cold atoms", Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022047 (2026-06-11), DOI 10.1103/1h9j-df4k
locators: HTML v2: abstract; Eqs. (1)–(6); Figs. 1–4 discussion; conclusion; especially signed Eq. (3) definition of τ, Eq. (3) discussion, and note below Fig. 2 distinguishing bright-sector entropy from total mini-universe entropy
assumptions: About 2.4×10^4 87Rb atoms in conservative optical trap; thin barrier partitions bright/observed and dark/unobserved sectors; negligible measured dissipation/loss on ~100 ms timescale; reduced mean-field bright-sector model; experimentally estimated coarse-grained Shannon entropy per particle s for bright sector and chosen scalar field φ; S=Ns and τ=(σ/k_B)∫(dS/dφ)|dφ|, retaining the sign of dS/dφ. Effective Schrödinger equation further uses M(φ)=αφ, Feshbach–Villars decomposition, positive onward-in-time branch and a Taylor approximation.
conclusion: Author reports that τ orders observed-sector data across expansion/recollapse, growing monotonically almost everywhere but showing a few wiggles where dS and dφ change sign in coarse sampling. Eq. (3) uses |dφ| but retains the sign of dS/dφ, so it does not guarantee monotonicity. Bright-sector S=Ns is approximately proportional to bright-sector atom number because s stays order unity; separately, total mini-universe entropy is reported constant within experimental errors. A derived effective Schrödinger equation reproduces measured width data in a selected low-barrier case.
proof_status: Primary arXiv HTML full text inspected; equation and experiment claims read; no data reanalysis or independent reproduction.
dependencies: Page–Wootters and Wheeler–DeWitt relational-time motivation; cold-atom mean-field reduction; coarse-grained Shannon entropy; chosen clock field and branch selection.
open_questions: Does the signed entropy-derived ordering add a nontrivial prediction beyond the observed atom-number/field trajectory? Does another internal clock produce distinguishable outcomes? Is the analog correspondence sufficient to transfer anything to cosmological WDW systems?
relevance: Recent measured relational/entropic clock proposal with a detailed apparatus and stated model bridge.
limits: A laboratory analog benchmarks a clock construction for this engineered subsystem, not the ontology of cosmological time. Entropy flow/time ordering is not by itself objective passage; thermodynamic arrow and temporal ontology remain distinct. The published version has a different title (Crossref, checked 2026-10-20); only arXiv v2 was read, so differences in the published text are unaudited.

title: Post-Newtonian Parameters and Constraints on Einstein-Aether Theory
locators: APS abstract only; detailed action, parameter mapping, and joint bounds not audited here
assumptions: Einstein-aether gravity: generally covariant metric theory coupled to a dynamical unit timelike vector field, with couplings that select a local preferred timelike structure and break local Lorentz symmetry.
conclusion: Authors compute post-Newtonian parameters and combine them with observational and theoretical constraints including vacuum Cherenkov, nucleosynthesis, stability, and positive energy. The timed preferred structure is physically coupled; it is not merely an undetectable metaphysical foliation.
proof_status: Abstract-level source inspection only; equations and parameter-space results not independently checked.
dependencies: Parameterized post-Newtonian expansion and Einstein-aether action/couplings.
open_questions: Extract the exact allowed coupling region and compare with newer gravity-wave and pulsar constraints before making a model-level exclusion statement.
relevance: Named preferred-structure model showing how a foliation-like field can enter measurable dynamics.
limits: A bound on Einstein-aether parameters is not a bound on every preferred foliation, presentism, or moving spotlight. An empirically hidden foliation with no couplings is a distinct model class.

title: Local Lorentz Invariance Test with the LAGEOS Satellites
version: Phys. Rev. D 114, 024072 (2026), published 2026-07-27; DOI 10.1103/hj6p-bfyr; companion Letter Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 051401 (2026)
locators: APS abstract; satellite test uses LAGEOS/LAGEOS II orbital mean argument of latitude over almost three decades; preferred-frame direction taken from CMB; PPN α1
assumptions: Weak-field PPN interpretation; a preferred CMB-aligned gravitational frame contributes through α1 (GR predicts α1=0); orbital and satellite force modeling over nearly 30 years.
conclusion: Authors report α1 constrained to approximately 2×10^-5, improving a previous lunar-laser-ranging limit. This tests a preferred-frame dynamical coupling in gravity and constrains model parameter space; it does not test a bare metaphysical/global-now structure.
proof_status: Primary APS abstract checked; full orbit solution/systematics and statistical analysis not independently audited.
dependencies: PPN framework, CMB-defined candidate frame, satellite laser ranging and orbital perturbation model.
open_questions: Translate α1 confidence/likelihood into explicit exclusions for named Einstein-aether coupling branches using the paper's full tables; examine correlated nuisance/systematic parameters.
relevance: Current quantitative preferred-frame test with model-specific observable and nonzero sensitivity.
limits: Null constraint (not evidence for a frame); effects depend on the PPN sector. GR plus a hidden, uncoupled foliation retains identical predictions by stipulation. No ontology follows from α1 alone.

title: Lorentz and CPT Tests with Clock-Comparison Experiments
locators: HTML full text: Sec. II theory and boosts; Sec. III.1–III.4 clock/comagnetometer applications; Tables 5, 6, 9, 10, 13, 14; Appendix B frame transformation
assumptions: Standard-Model Extension (SME) Lorentz/CPT-violating operators; atomic structure approximated with independent-particle electronic model and Schmidt nuclear model; coefficients fixed in approximately inertial Sun-centered frame; lab orientation/boost generates sidereal/annual frequency modulation; coefficient interpretation depends on sector and adopted nuclear/electronic matrix elements.
conclusion: Authors derive spectral shifts for clock/comagnetometer families and reinterpret existing data into minimal and nonminimal SME coefficient constraints; different systems are complementary. This empirically tests specific particle-sector Lorentz-violating dynamics, not a temporal ontology label.
proof_status: Primary full HTML read at stated sections/tables; no recomputation of coefficient extraction or reanalysis of experimental raw data.
dependencies: SME; atomic/nuclear structure models; Sun-centered frame conventions; prior experimental data and uncertainty reports.
open_questions: Update selected matter-sector limits against post-2018 data-table revisions and exact independent coefficient combinations; do not quote a scalar bound where only correlated combinations are measured.
relevance: Actual clock-comparison route from observable frequencies to named physical model parameters.
limits: Bounds apply to specified SME coefficients under stated material-model assumptions; preserving Lorentz-invariant observable dynamics while adding an uncoupled preferred foliation is outside this inference. Sidereal modulation can indicate anisotropic dynamics without implying objective passage. Coordinator correction 2026-10-20: the authors are Kostelecký and Vargas (arXiv listing), not Kostelecký and Mewes; the stable ID keeps the old name.

title: Tests of Relativity by Complementary Rotating Michelson-Morley Experiments
locators: APS abstract; dual active-rotation cavity experiments ran for more than one year; optical Fabry–Perot fused-silica resonators in Berlin and microwave sapphire whispering-gallery resonators in Perth
assumptions: Resonator frequency orientation dependence is mapped to SME photon/electron coefficients; the simultaneous limits depend on the analyzed coefficient sector/model and cavity materials.
conclusion: Authors report simultaneous limits on five electron and eight photon Lorentz-violating coefficients down to 10^-16, improving prior work by factors 3–50.
proof_status: Primary APS abstract inspected; full analysis, coefficient covariance, and experimental data not audited.
dependencies: Michelson–Morley resonator comparison; SME mapping and material-response calculations.
open_questions: Inspect the full covariance and assumptions behind the quoted simultaneous sector limits; later experiments may supersede their sensitivity.
relevance: Direct preferred-anisotropy/boost discriminator for specified physical propagation models.
limits: Bounds on selected SME coefficients do not constrain every Lorentz-violating theory and do not measure ontology or objective passage. Note: first author is H. Müller; the stable ID names a later co-author.

title: Quantum Signatures of Proper Time in Optical Ion Clocks
locators: APS full text: abstract, Formalism, SODS, vSODS, time-dilation-induced entanglement, qSODS, conclusions; supplemental protocol referenced for extracting quantum SODS
assumptions: Harmonically trapped optical ion clock; low-energy Hamiltonian couples internal clock energy to motional degrees via relativistic proper-time corrections; proposal uses strongly squeezed motion and Ramsey interferometry; system-specific trapped-ion state preparation/readout and control assumed.
conclusion: Authors derive vacuum-energy and squeezing-related second-order Doppler shifts plus quantum corrections, and propose observing clock-motion entanglement through visibility reduction and frequency shifts in state-of-the-art ion clocks. The APS paper states these effects would require a quantum description of proper-time dynamics beyond the usual classical parameter treatment.
proof_status: Published full-text sections and abstract inspected; proposed signal calculation not independently reproduced and experimental observation not claimed.
dependencies: Relativistic low-energy clock Hamiltonian; quantum metrology/Ramsey protocol; trapped-ion squeezing and readout feasibility; standard quantum dynamics.
open_questions: What are the achieved versus projected squeezing, coherence, and systematic-error requirements in the supplemental protocol? Does the signal discriminate quantum proper-time coupling from alternative effective Hamiltonians?
relevance: Concrete proposed quantum-clock observable that could favor a physical dynamical package over a classical-proper-time approximation.
limits: No data yet establishes the proposed effect. Even if observed, it would select or constrain clock-dynamics models; quantum proper-time superposition does not by itself establish temporal ontology, objective passage, or indeterminism.

title: Interference of Clocks: A Quantum Twin Paradox
locators: PMC full text: Introduction, Eqs. (1)–(3), Results on time dilation/gravito-kick action, Conclusions
assumptions: Single atomic clock in a superposition of paths of a closed light-pulse atom interferometer; proper-time phase approximated in weak-field/low-velocity regime; specific pulse geometry and recoil protocol; signal via path distinguishability and output fringe visibility.
conclusion: Authors show a specific interferometer geometry can encode special-relativistic time-dilation difference and produce visibility loss, while their light-pulse geometry is insensitive to gravitational time dilation because the proper-time difference is independent of the gravitational field in the freely falling frame. It is a proposed quantum-clock interferometry realization, not an ontology test.
proof_status: Primary full text and key equations read; no experimental reproduction or numerical sensitivity study here.
dependencies: Weak-field proper-time expansion, atom optics, pulse phase/action accounting, coordinate invariance.
open_questions: Which feasible geometries isolate gravitational rather than kinematic proper-time differences, and what systematics dominate?
relevance: Important concrete positive case: an observable can select between physical clock-dynamics models once preparation, trajectory coupling, and readout are specified.
limits: Tests relativistic clock dynamics and interferometer geometry. Any ontology consequence needs a separate bridge premise; a different path proper time is not evidence for a moving present.

title: Testing Local Lorentz Invariance with Laser Tracking of the LAGEOS and LAGEOS II Satellites
locators: APS full text: abstract; Orbit determination and residuals; Measurement and constraint; Table II systematic error budget; conclusion
assumptions: Weak-field PPN test of α1 using CMB-aligned candidate preferred-frame direction; phase-sensitive annual signal in LAGEOS/LAGEOS II mean argument of latitude; independent GEODYN II and SATAN orbit reductions over about 28.3 and 31.4 years; uncertainties separate statistical estimates from a root-sum-square systematic budget.
conclusion: Paper reports α1=(+2±3)×10^-5 for GEODYN II and (+1±2)×10^-5 for SATAN, with those ± values statistical standard deviations; they are compatible with α1=0. Table II gives total systematic RSS σ_sys≈7.7×10^-6. The abstract summarizes the result as a new constraint |α1|~2×10^-5. This is not itself a stated confidence-level upper limit; do not present the abstract scale as a precise 95% bound.
proof_status: Primary APS full text inspected at the stated sections and table; orbit reduction and significance not independently reproduced.
dependencies: PPN α1 mapping; CMB reference velocity/direction; satellite laser ranging; GEODYN II and SATAN precise-orbit-determination packages; modeled gravitational and non-gravitational perturbations.
open_questions: The paper points to companion PRD material for parameter-space bounds; an independent analysis should inspect its coupling-space mapping and full covariance/systematic model before quoting exclusions.
relevance: Full-text review of the numerical interpretation behind the abstract-level 2026 LAGEOS preferred-frame result.
limits: An estimate near zero with statistical and systematic errors constrains a coupled PPN preferred-frame effect; it is not a detection and does not test a causally idle hidden foliation or an ontology label.
